statements.t: While the cost of our Class II conventional milk decreased minimally in the third quarter of 2026 as compared to the second quarter of 2026, we currently anticipate our average price per pound for conventional milk will be higher in the fourth quarter as compared to the third quarter of 2026.

In addition, the elevated costs we experienced in the second quarter of 2026 of resin-based packaging such as bottles and caps, as well as ingredients and transportation costs continued during the third quarter of 2026, and we currently expect the price of these inputs will continue at elevated levels during the fourth quarter of 2026.
We do not currently expect tariffs to have a material adverse impact on our operations or financial results.

The Company remains in a strong financial position, and believes that its cash flow from operations, revolving credit facility, interim funding agreement, and cash and cash equivalents will continue to provide sufficient liquidity for its working capital needs, capital resource requirements, and growth initiatives and to ensure the continuation of the Company as a going concern.
We are in compliance with the terms of the Credit Agreement and expect to meet foreseeable financial requirements.
The success of our business and financing strategies will continue to provide us with the financial flexibility to take advantage of various opportunities as they arise.

The project will be funded primarily through cash on-hand and cash flow from operations, with further requirements available under the Company’s revolving credit facility and interim funding agreement.
We expect to be able to manufacture and package at an increased scale beginning in Q1 2027, with completion of the project expected to occur during Q2 2027.

Smolyansky continued, “Profitability this quarter continued to reflect an elevated input cost environment, and while we expect the cost pressure to persist in the fourth quarter, our outlook for 2027 has not changed.
We expect the planned price increases across our portfolio to take effect with distributors and retailers on a rolling basis through the end of the year and into the first quarter of 2027.
With our pricing actions and the productivity gains we anticipate from our capacity investments, we expect gross margin expansion and improved profitability in 2027.
We are well on pace to shatter our annual net sales record in 2026, and look forward to extending our category leadership and building on this momentum as we look ahead to 2027.”

A live conference call and Q&A session with management discussing these results with additional comments and details will be made available through the “Investor Relations” section of the Company’s website at https://lifewaykefir.com/webinars-reports/ at 4:30 p.m.
